title: Driver app onboarding pain for seasonal drivers
gist: Aisha details why new seasonal drivers struggle with the driver app: email-and-code login, location permissions that break tracking, and no way to practice before a live route. Asher connects it to Priya's onboarding redesign and asks for Brightside drivers to test it; Jordan notes the tension with live ETA for Q4 capacity.

turns.t: Okay, so Aisha, that's actually a good handoff to you. Asher mentioned the driver onboarding work, and I know you've had some things you wanted to raise about the driver app. I'd love to just hear it, unfiltered.

Yeah. Okay. So, unfiltered. The app is fine once a driver knows it. My experienced drivers, honestly, they like it, they don't think about it. The problem is new drivers, and specifically seasonal drivers. We staff up every year from mid-November through New Year's, Thanksgiving is our biggest week by a mile, and this year we're bringing on about forty-five seasonal drivers across the three metros. A lot of them have never driven for a delivery company. Some of them are, you know, college kids home for the holidays, some are retirees picking up shifts. And the first day with the app is rough.
Can you walk me through where it goes wrong? Like literally step by step, if you can.

Sure. So step one is login. Right now it's an email plus a company code. Our seasonal folks don't get a Brightside email, so they use their personal one, and half of them mistype it when we set them up, or they use a different one when they log in, and then they're locked out on their first morning, standing in the depot at six a.m., and a dispatcher has to stop what they're doing to sort it out. That alone, last November, I think we had something like a dozen lockouts in the first week.
Mm-hm.

Then permissions. Especially on Android. The phone asks, do you want to allow location all the time, only while using the app, or don't allow. And a new driver doesn't know what that means, so they tap only while using, because that sounds safer. And then they switch over to make a phone call or open the camera for a proof of delivery photo, and tracking just stops, and on our dispatch screen the van looks like it's parked for twenty minutes. And then dispatch calls them to ask if they're okay. Which, again, phone ringing while driving.
Yeah, we've seen that one on a couple of other accounts too.

And then the big one is the first route is real. There's no practice. Their first ever stop in the app is a real customer with real groceries. So they don't know how to mark a stop as customer not home, they don't know how to do a substitution note, they don't know that you can swipe to see the next three stops. And they panic a little, and they slow down, and they call dispatch. The experienced drivers end up training them in the parking lot, which, that's half a day of a good driver not driving.
What about proof of delivery? Is the photo step a problem, or is that one okay?

It's okay once they find it. The problem is it's two taps deep, so new people complete the stop without the photo, and then they get flagged, and then we get a dispute from the customer three days later saying their bags never showed up and we have no photo. That's maybe a smaller thing. But it's the same pattern, it's stuff that's obvious to someone who's done two hundred routes and invisible to someone on their first.
Yeah. Okay. I'm writing that one down, I don't think it's in the redesign yet.
And they quit. That's the part that costs me. We spend money recruiting them, we do the background check, and then they have one bad morning and don't come back.

Yeah. Last year we onboarded thirty-two seasonal drivers, and I think eleven of them never finished their first route. Or quit within the first, no, sorry, it was twelve. Twelve didn't make it through the first week. Some of that is just seasonal work, people flake. But a lot of it is that first morning.

Okay, so this is really helpful, and it lines up almost exactly with what we're seeing across all our customers. Across the board, about thirty-eight percent of new drivers drop off before they complete their first route. Our goal for Q4 is to get that below fifteen. Priya, who leads design on our side, has a redesign of the onboarding flow, and the three main pieces are basically your list. Login by phone number with a text code instead of email plus company code. A short permissions primer, three screens, that explains in plain language why the app needs location all the time before the phone asks the scary question. And a practice route, so a new driver can run through five fake stops in the depot, including a customer not home and a substitution, before they ever touch a real order.
Oh, okay. Yeah. That's — honestly, if you'd asked me to write the list, that's the list.

So my ask would be, would you be open to having a few of your drivers test it with Priya? Ideally new ones. Even four or five people. She'd do it in person or over video, half an hour each, and it'd be on the prototype, so nothing touches your live routes.

Yes. Absolutely. We have an early cohort of seasonal hires starting the third week of October, before the big wave. I could probably get you four or five of them. And I'll send over what I've got from last year too, I have a spreadsheet of the support tickets and the stuff dispatchers wrote down, it's messy but it's real.
Messy and real is perfect. I'll connect you and Priya this week.

Can I just, I want to make sure I understand. Earlier you said live ETA and this onboarding work are competing for the same people in Q4. So if you do this, are you telling me you're not doing live ETA?

It's a fair question. It's not quite either-or, but it is a real trade-off, and I'd rather be honest about it than pretend we have infinite engineers. Both of them pull on the same mobile and frontend folks. We're also hiring for exactly that right now, two senior frontend engineers, but realistically those people don't help us in Q4. So what I'm working out this week is the sequencing. That's part of why I want to give you a real date on the ninth and not a fast one.
I'll be honest, I want both.
I mean, for me, in November, onboarding matters more. If I lose twelve drivers in Thanksgiving week again, a tracking link doesn't help anybody, because the groceries aren't on a van.
Noted, Aisha. Thank you.
Just saying.
No, it's genuinely useful for us to hear both of those, because they're both real. And it's good input for Friday.
Okay. Point taken. I still want both. But point taken.

title: Sacramento expansion, renewal and next steps
gist: Jordan says Brightside plans a fourth metro in Sacramento with about 60 more vans in Q1, but awarding it to Tandem depends on reliability and live ETA; Sofia proposes folding Sacramento into the Jan 31 renewal, and the call closes with a recap of commitments and clear stakes.

turns.t: So I want to make sure we have real time for the last piece. Jordan, last time we talked you mentioned Sacramento. Where are you on that?

Yeah. So, Sacramento is happening. We signed the lease on the depot two weeks ago. We're planning to launch in Q1, probably late February if construction behaves, and the plan is about sixty vans to start. Which gets us to two-forty total. And I'll be direct with you about where that sits. I'd like to run Sacramento on Tandem. It's easier for us, one system, Aisha's team already knows it, our dispatchers know it. That's the default. But I have to make that call by mid-December, because we need to train people in January, and it's contingent on two things.
Okay.

One is reliability. I need October and November to be clean. If we have another twenty-fourth, especially in Thanksgiving week, I can't go to my CEO and say let's put another sixty vans on the same platform. I just can't. And two is live ETA. Sacramento is a new market for us, we're going to be competing with people who already have tracking links, and I'm not launching a new metro without one. So if the date you send me on the ninth is, I don't know, next summer, then I have to look at whether we run Sacramento on something else. I don't want to. But I would.
That's clear. And honestly, I appreciate you telling us straight instead of us finding out in December.

I'd rather tell you now. You've been good partners for two years. The numbers this quarter are proof of that. I'm not looking for an excuse to leave. I'm telling you what I need to be able to stay and grow.
And on reliability, what do I actually tell my CEO? Like, beyond the things you listed from the retro. Because he's going to say, how do you know it won't happen again in Thanksgiving week.

Two things you can tell him. One, we're going to start deliberately failing over that cache cluster every month, in a controlled way, so we find out how the system reacts on a Tuesday afternoon that we picked, not on a busy morning that we didn't. And two, we're going to put a change freeze around Thanksgiving week, no risky deploys to the dispatch or ETA paths that week. I can't promise you nothing will ever break. Nobody honest can. But I can promise that if it does, it breaks smaller, and you hear from us first.
Okay. The freeze, I like. Put that in writing in the incident report, if you can.

I'll put it in. And Aisha, on that, it'd help us to have your Thanksgiving week volume forecast. Orders per day, and how many vans you're running per metro. If we know the peak, we can make sure we're watching the right things that week.
Yeah, I can get you that. It's usually about one point six times a normal week, but I'll get the real forecast from planning. They do it by metro.

Which ties into the renewal, so let me put that on the table. Your renewal is January thirty-first. What I'd like to propose is that we don't treat those as two separate conversations. Rather than renewing the hundred and eighty vans in January and then doing a separate expansion contract for Sacramento in February, we fold Sacramento into the renewal. One agreement, two-forty vans, with the Sacramento vans starting whenever the depot goes live. That's simpler for your procurement and it means the pricing reflects the bigger footprint from day one.
I'm open to that. What does pricing look like?

I'm not going to throw a number out on this call, because I'd rather get it right than get it fast. But I'll put together a proposal for the combined renewal, with volume pricing at two-forty vans, and I'd want to have it to you in early November, after you've seen the roadmap and the live ETA date. That way you're evaluating the whole thing at once, not a price in isolation.
That's fine. Early November works. My CFO's going to want to see the renewal number next to the Sacramento number anyway, so having them together actually helps me.

Perfect. And would you be able to send us the Sacramento timeline and the van count? Even rough. Just so we can start planning the setup, the depot geofence, the zones, that kind of thing, and not be scrambling in February.
Yeah, I can do that. I've got a launch plan doc, I'll strip out the internal stuff, the lease terms and whatever, and send you the dates and the van count. Probably next week.
That'd be great, thank you.

And on our side, if Sacramento goes ahead, I'd want to launch it on Routing v3 from day one rather than migrating later. GA is November seventeenth, so by late February it'll have a few months of mileage on it. That's something we can show you in the roadmap too.
Okay. Yeah, that makes sense. No point launching on the old thing.
And if Sacramento's on the new onboarding flow from the start, that's sixty vans' worth of brand new drivers. That would be the best test you could ask for, honestly.
That's a really good point. Yeah.

Okay, so I want to recap, because there's a lot here and I want to make sure we all walk away with the same list. On our side. I'm applying the service credit, ten percent of one month, to your October invoice. I'm adding you and Aisha to direct incident notifications by text, today. I'm sending you the written incident report by Friday, with the Thanksgiving change freeze in it. Asher is sending the Q4 roadmap with a specific date for live ETA sharing by October ninth, and I'll set up a call right after to walk through it. Asher's connecting Aisha with Priya this week for the driver testing. And I'll have a combined renewal and Sacramento proposal to you in early November. On your side, Aisha's sending the seasonal driver feedback spreadsheet and lining up four or five drivers from the October cohort, plus the Thanksgiving volume forecast. And Jordan, you're sending the Sacramento timeline and van count. Did I miss anything?
No, I think that's it. I'd just add one thing to yours, which is, if anything happens with the platform between now and then, you call me. Not the status page. You.
Me. Promise. And you've got my cell.
And mine, if Sofia's not picking up.

Okay. Look, I'll say this and then we can all go. I want this to work. I mean that. The Q3 numbers are good and Aisha's team likes the product. But between now and December, I need October to go cleanly, I need a real date for live ETA, and I need to not be surprised again. If those three things happen, I think Sacramento's an easy call.
That's really clear, and thank you for being so direct about it. It makes our job easier, honestly.
Agreed. Thanks, Jordan. Thanks, Aisha. You'll have the roadmap on the ninth.
Thanks, everyone. I'll email Priya once you intro us.
Thanks all. Talk soon.
Bye, have a good rest of your day.
